options: A Flow element that pauses for user input
A trigger that fires when a record is deleted
Apex code reaching outside the org to talk to another system over the network
A SOQL query that spans more than one object
questions.explain: A callout is Apex making an outbound HTTP or SOAP request to a system outside Salesforce, and waiting within limits for a response.

questions.q: Which two callout families does Apex support?
options: Synchronous and Batch
Inbound and Platform Event
REST and GraphQL
HTTP and SOAP
questions.explain: Apex supports HTTP callouts (Http/HttpRequest/HttpResponse, typically REST/JSON) and SOAP callouts (built from a WSDL-generated class).

questions.q: What happens if Apex code tries to make a callout in the same transaction where it has already performed a DML insert, with nothing else changed?
options: It throws a runtime error, because a callout can't run with pending uncommitted DML in the same transaction
The DML is automatically rolled back and the callout proceeds
The callout silently fails and returns a null HttpResponse
It succeeds, but logs a warning in the debug log
questions.explain: A transaction can't make a callout while it has pending, uncommitted DML, async work, or email in that same transaction — this throws a runtime error rather than failing silently.

questions.q: Historically, what had to be configured in Setup before Apex could call out to an arbitrary external URL?
options: A Platform Event definition
A Remote Site Setting allow-listing the destination
A Change Data Capture channel
An Apex REST @RestResource annotation
questions.explain: Before Named Credentials became the modern standard, administrators added destinations to Remote Site Settings so Apex was permitted to reach them.

questions.q: Why does Salesforce enforce the rule against making a callout alongside pending DML in the same transaction?
options: Because HTTP callouts always take exactly 120 seconds to complete
Because SOAP callouts are deprecated and no longer supported
Because a callout is a real network round-trip to a system Salesforce doesn't control, and the platform doesn't want an open, uncommitted transaction locking rows while it waits
Because only Batch Apex is allowed to perform DML
questions.explain: The rule protects against a slow or unresponsive external system holding an uncommitted transaction and its row locks open indefinitely.
